tests.name: native lexical query preserves phrases, boolean operators, regex and filters
ACL applies before matches, graph references, context and pagination
SQLite parity and stale update/delete fallback preserve canonical results
generated navigation preserves authored content and canonical snippet lines
FTS trigram path preserves substring, short term and quoted punctuation parity
bounded retrieval equals scoring everything (hits, order, snippets, cursor) for common terms, phrases, regex, offsets and tiny/large limits
a frequent term with a small limit reads a small fraction of the matching documents; rare terms and large limits still read what they must
exact page boundary: with exactly `limit` matches there is no cursor, with one more there is
query engine pushes the page bound down to retrieval and returns the same rows
HTTP embedder: request shape, batching, ordering, retries with backoff, and strict response validation
HTTP embedder: timeouts, cancellation, redirects, oversize responses and transport errors are bounded and sanitized
createEmbedder / describeEmbedding: validation, defaults and key handling; nothing is built unless configured
end to end over real HTTP and the CLI: embed sync, semantic search, auto becomes hybrid, status and capabilities, keyword unaffected
golden corpus, SQLite OFF: every query returns exactly the authorized golden set and never private/tombstoned data
golden corpus, SQLite ON: every query returns exactly the authorized golden set and never private/tombstoned data
SQLite and filesystem return identical sets (and snippets) for every golden query
stale index: commits, edits and deletes after the last rebuild are never silently missing; health reports staleness
corrupt, truncated or deleted SQLite files: queries stay correct via fallback, rebuild restores the index, integrity checks pass
killing the process during an index rebuild leaves canonical data intact and the next rebuild succeeds
ACL is applied before counts, cursors and snippets on both backends
seed 11: ripgrep, raw-file scan and SQLite equal the full-corpus oracle (ids, revisions, lines, scores, snippets)
seed 4242: ripgrep, raw-file scan and SQLite equal the full-corpus oracle (ids, revisions, lines, scores, snippets)
seed 90210: ripgrep, raw-file scan and SQLite equal the full-corpus oracle (ids, revisions, lines, scores, snippets)
parsed immutable revisions carry exact LF/CRLF body offsets through Vault visibility
journal overlay: create, update, tombstone, purge and restore after the checkpoint are served correctly, lag is reported, sync converges to rebuild
damaged, foreign-format or inconsistent index databases degrade only their own scope, never correctness
authorization is evaluated per query: grants and revocations apply immediately, objects skipped earlier appear after a grant, outsiders see nothing
persisted manifest is only trusted when it provably belongs to this journal; damaged or foreign files are rebuilt, not believed
concurrent writers and readers: every committed document becomes findable, no reader errors, no unauthorized hit
killing the process during sync, rebuild or manifest save leaves canonical data intact and the next query correct
disabled by default: semantic and hybrid are unavailable, keyword/grep/regex/auto work, and the mode that ran is reported
semantic and hybrid REQUIRE the SQLite index: without it they are disabled even with an embedding provider, while keyword and grep stay fully functional
SQLite on but no vectors yet: not ready until "embed sync"; then semantic finds what no keyword shares; keyword matches are unaffected
hybrid fuses keyword and semantic rankings by reciprocal rank fusion; an exact keyword match is never suppressed; auto becomes hybrid when ready
regex and exact grep never touch the vector backend; keyword is lexical when SQLite is off, BM25 when on
ACL: semantic and hybrid never return unreadable objects, never let them influence ranking, and report lag only for readable objects
revision consistency: stale vectors are ignored and reported as lag, new text is found by keyword at once and by meaning after sync, deletes vanish
privacy: a remote embedding service never receives workspace text unless allowed; the skipped objects are counted, global knowledge is embedded

failure handling: embedding outage makes semantic/hybrid fail with a sanitized error, auto degrades to a labelled keyword result, partial sync leaves a consistent index, a model change never mixes vectors
immutability and cleanup: embedding and searching never change the journal or revisions; purge removes vectors
corrupt or foreign vector data is ignored, never trusted: garbage rows, wrong dimensions and a damaged database fall back to keyword with an honest status
query engine: semantic/hybrid/auto through the typed AST report the mode that ran; unavailable without the backend unless a labelled downgrade is requested
optional sqlite-vec acceleration returns the same ranking as the portable scan; when the extension is absent the portable scan is used and reported

gaps.reason: Building 100k documents through the fsynced commit protocol takes hours; 1k and 10k are measured. Bounded evaluation (tests/search/bounded.test.ts) reads a small fraction of matches for small pages; its effect at 10k/100k has NOT been re-measured since the change.

gaps.item: Semantic and hybrid retrieval quality with a real embedding model
gaps.reason: Mechanics, ACLs, revision consistency, privacy and failure handling are tested with a deterministic concept embedder and a real local HTTP server speaking the OpenAI embeddings protocol. No real model was evaluated, so retrieval quality is not claimed. Semantic/hybrid exist only with SQLite enabled and a configured provider.

Run with ENGRAM_SQLITE_VEC pointing at the extension (passed once on macOS arm64 during development); otherwise the portable scan is used and tested. Neither path is an approximate index: both scan all accepted vectors.
Brute-force scan cost grows linearly; no benchmark has been run (deferred by request).
Databases use WAL; rebuild-kill and corruption cases ran, a dedicated concurrent checkpoint stress did not.

Filesystem parity is exact. With SQLite, keyword results are ordered by FTS5 BM25 (reported as ranking: bm25): result sets, revisions, lines and snippets are compared with the oracle, the order is checked to follow the reported score, and no relevance-quality evaluation was done.

gaps.item: Files edited outside the API during search
gaps.reason: Covered for reconciliation (storage tests); not combined with search in this suite.

limitations: Filesystem and SQLite engines were compared on 19 golden queries over ASCII, CJK, accents, emoji, punctuation, code fences, frontmatter lookalikes, duplicate titles, tombstones and permission boundaries.
Both modes run the full golden corpus; the --no-sqlite functional suite is the default configuration of every other suite.
